subject.title: [Feature]: Skill author-defined setup hook (run skill-supplied script on install/update)

question: Should OpenClaw own an automatic skill-authored install/update setup hook, or should setup execution remain an external/admin plugin plus narrower SDK helpers?
rationale: The requested behavior adds host code execution during skill installation and update, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent core, plugin, consent, and security boundary.

options.title: Design core lifecycle contract
options.body: Add a reviewed install/update setup API with explicit consent, env allowlist, sandbox/path policy, logs, timeout ownership, failure handling, docs, and compatibility tests.

options.title: Keep setup external
options.body: Treat the published ClawHub plugin as the supported path and close core lifecycle work after documenting the manual/admin workflow and its limits.

options.title: Defer to SDK helper issue
options.body: Keep this issue linked to the broader installed-skill SDK helper work and postpone automatic lifecycle execution until that API direction is settled.

recommendation.title: Design core lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Add a reviewed install/update setup API with explicit consent, env allowlist, sandbox/path policy, logs, timeout ownership, failure handling, docs, and compatibility tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Most connected to current skill install and security-sensitive ClawHub installation paths in recent history.
